newsitem.title: CHILE: Rain cuts road to Codelco's Salvador copper mine.
newsitem.headline: Rain cuts road to Codelco's Salvador copper mine.

text.p: The main road to Codelco's Salvador copper mine in northern Chile has been cut by heavy rains and landslides but operations at the mine are working normally, a spokesman said.
Employees at Phelps Dodge's Candelaria mine also reported unspecified problems at the mine associated with the rain.
They said managers were evaluating the problems at the mine outside Copiapo and would comment later.

A Codelco spokesman said the road to Salvador from Copiapo has been out of service due to heavy rain and landslides since Thursday, when an unusual rainstorm lashed the Third Region, an important copper mining area.

Road connections between the mine and smelter at Potrerillos were normal, as were operations at the roughly 100,000-tonne-a-year mine, said the spokesman in Santiago. Officials at the mine itself could not be reached for comment.

Highways throughout northern Chile were cut by the weather, including the country's main north-south route near the city of La Serena. Authorities said they expected transport to return to normal on the main motorway Friday.

Operations and transport at Chuquicamata, farther north, were normal, said the spokesman. He also denied rumors of an earth tremor at Chuquicamata, as did the National Emergency Office which said it had no news at all of a tremor in the area.
